t: You're looking at Thomas More House, a mid-rise terrace block on the Barbican Estate. Its name honours Sir Thomas More, the English lawyer, statesman and Renaissance humanist. He served Henry VIII as Lord Chancellor from 1529 to 1532, and the Catholic Church venerates him as a martyr and saint. He also wrote Utopia, published in 1516, which describes the political system of an imaginary island state. So the block carries the name of a man known as much for his writing as for his public career.
